title: Three P0 cards taught a conditional rule as an absolute one: EIAPP invalidation, ISO 19030 scope, hydrostatic-table validity, and an ISM critical-equipment list that read as universal
candidate_claim: Founder/GPT independently inspected the published repository at 9e26f02 - live card bytes plus authoritative external sources - and returned a bounded finding list. QB5_J#q2: the NOx Technical File proposition was equivalent to 'going outside the identified Technical File settings/components invalidates the EIAPP certificate', which is too absolute; and 'ISO 19030 is the standard method for separating hull fouling from engine deterioration' overstates the standard's scope. QB1_D#q7: the 60-second answer said that the moment the waterline is not parallel to the baseline, the hydrostatic tables stop being valid, which is too categorical. QB5_I#q8: the corrected ISM 10.3/10.4 logic was accepted, but the critical-equipment and critical-spares example lists, and the class spare-parts line, could read as a universal ISM-prescribed or universal Class-prescribed list.
candidate_verdict: UPHELD ON ALL FOUR PROPOSITIONS, AND NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS. None of the three cards contained a wrong fact; each stated a conditional rule in absolute terms, which is precisely the defect class no digest pin can see (SKILL.md 8.2a). The substance GPT accepted in each card is unchanged: QB5_J#q2's diagnostic spine, QB1_D#q7's entire Bonjean treatment, and QB5_I#q8's ISM 10.3/10.4 distinction from CORR-ISM-SPARES-20260902. Two sections of QB1_D#q7 were examined and DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE because they were already correct and are the formulation the others were brought into line with: the body heading 'Why the hydrostatic tables are not enough' with its paragraph, and the deep-dive that already said the tables 'assume even keel' and that every Bonjean situation is one 'where that assumption has failed'.

authority.nox_instrument: NOx Technical Code 2008, as carried in MARPOL Annex VI and NTC 2008 with Guidelines, 2023 Edition, held at 03-imo-instruments/MARPOL-Annex-VI/_base-and-amendments/MARPOL_Annex_VI_and_NOx_Technical_code_2008_5th_Ed_2023.pdf
authority.nox_access_note: THE HELD FILE IS AN IMAGE-ONLY SCAN. All 535 pages return an empty text layer, so the instrument recorded as held could not be read by any tool that had previously cited it. The provisions below were obtained by rendering the pages at 350 dpi and running OCR. Quoted wording is therefore reliable for substance and for locating provisions; it is not asserted as byte-verbatim.
authority.operative_text_2_4_1: To enable an Administration to perform the engine surveys described in 2.1, the technical file required by 2.3.4 shall, at a minimum, contain the following information: .1 identification of those components, settings and operating values of the engine that influence its NOx emissions including any NOx-reducing device or system; .2 identification of the full range of allowable adjustments or alternatives for the components of the engine; ... .7 specifications of those spare parts/components that, when used in the engine, according to those specifications, will result in continued compliance of the engine with the applicable NOx emission limit; and .8 the EIAPP Certificate, as applicable.
authority.operative_text_2_4_3_1: engine parameter check method in accordance with 6.2 to verify that an engine's component, setting and operating values have not deviated from the specifications in the engine's technical file
authority.operative_text_2_4_4: If the method differs from the verification procedure method specified in the technical file as originally approved, the procedure of the method needs to be either added as an amendment to the technical file or appended as an alternative to the procedure given in the technical file.
authority.operative_text_6_2_1_1: Engines that meet the following conditions shall be eligible for an engine parameter check method: .1 engines that have received a pre-certificate (EIAPP Certificate) on the test bed and those that received a certificate (EIAPP Certificate) following an initial certification survey in accordance with 2.2.4; and .2 engines that have undergone modifications or adjustments to the designated engine components and adjustable features since they were last surveyed.
authority.operative_text_6_2_1_2: When a marine diesel engine is designed to run within the applicable NOx emission limit, it is most likely that within the marine life of the engine, the NOx emission limit may be adhered to. The applicable NOx emission limit may, however, be contravened by adjustments or modification to the engine. Therefore, an engine parameter check method shall be used to verify whether the engine is still within the applicable NOx emission limit.
authority.operative_text_6_2_1_4: The purpose of such checks is to provide a ready means of determining that an engine is correctly adjusted in accordance with the manufacturer's specification and remains in a condition of adjustment consistent with the initial certification by the Administration as being in compliance with regulation 13 as applicable.
why_the_absolute_form_is_wrong: 2.4.1.2 requires the technical file to identify the FULL RANGE OF ALLOWABLE ADJUSTMENTS. An adjustment inside that declared range is expressly contemplated by the Code and cannot, on any reading, invalidate the certificate.

6.2.1.1.2 makes an engine that HAS ALREADY been modified or adjusted since its last survey ELIGIBLE for the engine parameter check method. The Code treats such an engine as a normal survey subject, not as one whose certificate has lapsed.

6.2.1.2 states the actual consequence: the limit MAY be contravened by adjustment, and the parameter check exists to VERIFY whether it has been. The operative risk is non-compliance with the applicable NOx limit and with the certified configuration, established at survey - not automatic loss of the EIAPP certificate.

NO NEW LEGAL EFFECT IS ASSERTED. The corrected wording claims strictly LESS than the wording it replaces: it names the approved-procedure/verification/survey route and the possibility of non-compliance, and stops there.
authority.iso_19030_scope: ISO 19030 is 'Ships and marine technology - Measurement of changes in hull and propeller performance'. Its subject is the hull and propeller. It does not assess machinery condition, and the separation of hull contribution from machinery deterioration is an inference drawn by reading its output against corrected engine-performance data - not something the standard performs. The card previously named one input as the whole method.
authority.hydrostatics: Tabulated hydrostatic particulars are computed for the ship upright and on even keel. They do not become 'invalid' when the waterline inclines - they remain a correct answer to the question they were computed for, and are simply not sufficient by themselves for an arbitrary inclined or heavily trimmed waterline, because every station is then at a different draught. Bonjean curves reconstruct the immersed sectional areas station by station for that actual waterline. The distinction is not pedantic: an examiner who hears 'invalid' hears a candidate who does not know what the tables are.
authority.ism_10_3_position: UNCHANGED FROM CORR-ISM-SPARES-20260902 AND RE-ASSERTED HERE. ISM 10.3 requires the Company to identify equipment and technical systems the sudden operational failure of which may result in hazardous situations, requires the SMS to provide specific measures promoting their reliability, and requires those measures to include regular testing of stand-by arrangements and equipment not in continuous use; 10.4 integrates 10.2's inspections and 10.3's measures into the ship's operational maintenance routine. The Code prescribes NO critical-equipment list, NO critical-spares list, NO minimum stock and NO reorder point. What 10.3 catches is therefore ship-specific, which is exactly what the corrected example lists now say.
authority.class_spares_position: There is no single universal classification-society spare-parts list. Required onboard spares for propulsion and essential auxiliaries differ between societies and with the ship's notation and machinery arrangement, and some arrangements attract reduced or no requirement. The card now conditions the claim on the vessel's own class rules and notation and tells the candidate to quote those rather than a universal list.

changed_propositions: Full answer: 'ISO 19030 is the standard method for separating hull and propeller deterioration from engine deterioration' -> ISO 19030 provides a framework for measuring changes in hull and propeller performance, which read with corrected engine-performance data is what lets you distinguish the hull and propeller contribution from machinery deterioration.

Cause list: hull and propeller 'separated by the ISO 19030 method' -> 'quantified by the ISO 19030 method, which measures the change in hull and propeller performance; set that against corrected engine data and the hull and propeller contribution separates out'.

Trap point: 'the components and settings identified in the NOx Technical File bound what may be adjusted, and going outside them invalidates the EIAPP certificate' -> the Technical File identifies the components, settings and operating values that influence NOx together with the full range of adjustments that are allowed; working outside the approved configuration goes down the approved route (amendment of the technical file, verification at survey by the engine parameter check method); an unapproved departure can leave the engine no longer compliant with its certified NOx configuration.

REG-BOX ISO 19030: 'the standard method for separating hull fouling from engine deterioration' -> 'Framework for measuring changes in hull and propeller performance; read together with corrected engine-performance data it helps distinguish the hull and propeller contribution from machinery deterioration. It does not itself assess engine condition'.

REG-BOX NOx: 'Bounds the identified components, settings and operating values that may be adjusted; going outside them invalidates the EIAPP certificate' -> 'Defines the engine's approved NOx-relevant components, settings and operating values, and the full range of allowable adjustments (NTC 2008 2.4.1). Departure from the approved configuration must follow the applicable approved procedure, verification or survey route; an unapproved departure can render the engine non-compliant with its certified NOx configuration'.
